lede: The Mantis sector with a name in it. Six or seven beacons open in combat before you can choose anything, one or two more skip the ship fight entirely and drop **2–4 boarders straight onto your deck**, and one beacon is always {{MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF}} — the only ship unlock either Mantis sector can hand you. Nothing here is settled at range.
callout: **Versus a plain Mantis Controlled Sector:** every list is the same list and every count is the same count — 6–7 hostile, 6–7 neutral, 1–2 boarding, 1–3 distress, 1–2 items, 1–2 stores, 2–3 empty. The entire difference is the guaranteed `MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF` beacon: one more jump on the map, one more event in the pool, and with it the sector's only ship unlock, its only named augment and its third quest start.

section_notes.MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF: Always placed, exactly once. It is a fight either way — the Mantis blue option is a greeting, not a way out — and everything it is worth comes after the shooting stops.
section_notes.HOSTILE_MANTIS: {{MANTIS_FIGHT}} is listed twice, so a plain Mantis warship is the likeliest thing waiting at any of these. {{DONOR_MANTIS_CHASE}} is the one that can leave the beacon unfinished — if it escapes, chasing it plants a quest marker; {{AUTO_WARNING}} is a Rebel scout that runs to report your position rather than fight to the end.
section_notes.BOARDERS_MANTIS: {{MANTIS_BOARDERS}} is listed twice against {{BOARDERS_SUN}}'s once. Neither is a ship battle you can decline: the boarders are aboard as the event opens, 2–4 of them, and the pirate version stages it inside a star's flare range.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_MANTIS: "Neutral" is a filing label. Five of these six can end in combat, {{MANTIS_CREW}} can kill a crew member and leave a Mantis loose in the room, and {{ALISON_MANTIS_CREW}} opens with an intruder already on deck.
section_notes.DISTRESS_BEACON_MANTIS: The densest pool on the page and the thinnest allocation. Three of the sector's four crew-killers live here, and so do six of its eleven gated events — the Rockman, Engi, Adv. Medbay, ion and drone answers all pay out in a pool that may only get one beacon.
section_notes.ITEMS: Trades and stations rather than free loot: {{REPAIR_STATION}}, {{REFUEL_STATION}} and the two selling posts all want something back, and {{TAVERN_HIRE}} is the one place in the sector that sells you a crew member outright.

steps.title: {{MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF}}
steps.detail: A Mantis ship under a century of bolted-on armour. Both choices end in the same fight — the **Mantis crew** option only buys an alien haka first, then charges the weapons anyway.

steps.title: Kill the crew, not the ship
steps.detail: Blowing the hull up pays a medium reward and ends it — "his death has left a great mystery unresolved." Everything below only exists on the branch where the ship survives and its crew does not.

steps.title: Find him alive
steps.detail: **Crew Teleporter** boards for survivors, **Sensors 3** scans for them; without either you just strip the wreck for a high reward. Hearing him out gives up his stash and pays high — that much needs no Medbay.

steps.title: Bring him back
steps.detail: **Adv. Medbay** or **Adv. Clone Bay** revives him and he joins: a Mantis with two levels in every skill, the **Mantis Pheromones** augment, high scrap, the stash marker, and coordinates for "a custom cruiser he has been working on" that unlock a ship.

steps.title: The stash
steps.detail: The marked beacon is a cache in an asteroid field, opened with his codes. No fight, no choice — a weapon.

items.text: The only two keys to the whole thief payout. Medbay 2 also opens the safe answer on {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}}.
Level 3 throughout: it finds the dying thief without boarding, reads {{BROKEN_REBEL_DRONE}} before you wake it, and adds a line at {{TRADER_UPGRADES}}.
Slips past the sleeping warship in {{MANTIS_FIGHT_CHOICE}} without a fight, and is graded at levels 1–3 on {{DISTRESS_SATELLITE_DEFENSE}}.
All four sit in the distress pool — {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} and {{DISTRESS_SATELLITE_DEFENSE}}. The crew that pays in the Mantis homeworlds is not Mantis.
Anti-Personnel, Boarding and Anti-Bio Beam each answer {{DISTRESS_INFESTATION}}; a System Repair Drone answers {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}.
One blue option in the entire sector needs a Mantis crew member, and it changes only the flavour text on {{MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF}}.

panels.title: Named things you can leave with

items.text: **Mantis Pheromones** — the only named item anywhere in the pool, and it comes off the thief.
**KazaaakplethKilik**, a Mantis with two levels in every skill, on the revive branch.
`unlockShip id="2"`, transmitted with the same handshake that hands you the crew and the augment.
Mantis from {{MANTIS_CREW}} and {{ALISON_MANTIS_CREW}}; the same escape pod can hold a human instead; {{TAVERN_HIRE}} sells one for scrap.
Two of the sector's three quest starts pay a weapon at the beacon they mark: the thief's `MANTIS_NAMED_THIEF_STASH`, and `DONOR_MANTIS_CHASE2` if you chase the collectors down.
Four events put hostiles inside your hull, and the map guarantees at least one boarding beacon. {{MANTIS_BOARDERS}} and {{BOARDERS_SUN}} arrive 2–4 strong with no ship fight attached.
Four events can kill a crew member outright: {{DISTRESS_INFESTATION}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}}, {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}}, and {{MANTIS_CREW}}, which kills **and** leaves the killer aboard.
Seven events in the pool open in combat and nine more can turn into it from a choice — and that is before the boarding pool, which never involves an enemy ship at all.
{{MANTIS_SUN_FIGHT}} and {{BOARDERS_SUN}} both stage next to a star, with the solar hazard running on your ship while you fight or repel.
{{TRAP_BEACON}} is a distress call that opens hostile, and siding with the fugitive in {{ALISON_MANTIS_CREW}} can cost hull and a system before the Engi ship even opens fire.
